speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what measures are taken to stop the illegal practice of carpooling arrangements set up via online chatgroups; and (b) whether the Ministry will embark on a public education campaign on allowable forms of carpooling in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Members of the public who come across individuals providing illegal car-pooling services may write to LTA or notify LTA through the OneMotoring portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I want to thank the Member for her suggestion for a campaign to improve public awareness of the allowable forms of car-pooling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will work with the taxi and private hire vehicle drivers' associations on this.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I declare that I am the advisor to the National Private Hire Vehicles Association, an affiliate association to the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The illegal practice of carpooling arrangement set up via online chatgroups continues to be an issue, creating safety concerns for passengers and affecting the professional reputation of licensed P2P drivers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Almost every minute, in these chats, there is an offer to or from a driver to carpool and offer from a passenger to hitch a ride.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that serious safety issues can come with the use of such unlicensed services – from the outrage of modesty to the most recent case of death where the driver did not even have a Class 3 licence – what more can the Ministry do to educate the public on the use of such services?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And would the Ministry consider also disallowing paid carpooling amongst strangers, even in matching platforms for the safety of all commuters?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for her supplementary questions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These operators are able to record the driver as well as the trip, check on the validity of the driver's licence and also enforce on the maximum two trips per day requirement.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This really is to protect the commuters or passengers' safety, provide the commuter with some safeguards.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is some value in providing or allowing some of these carpooling services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Because it optimises vehicle road capacity, the use of the vehicle, as well as, of course, reduce carbon footprint.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Totally banning carpooling services will not necessarily remove the problem.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If you look at the informal channels, as the Member has rightly pointed out, there is demand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, when there is demand, there is supply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And therefore I agree with the Member that besides enforcement actions through enforcement operations that we will continue to do, it is good to intensify our public education efforts to raise awareness among the public that their safety is not protected if they go through these informal channels, and that if they require such carpooling services, they should do it through the licensed or licence-exempt permitted operators.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will work with the associations to look at such a campaign.
